key_insight: The paper reformulates the full Boltzmann equation into coupled wave and particle components so the same exact system smoothly spans rarefied-gas kinetic behavior and continuum Navier–Stokes hydrodynamics.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical multiscale solver for CFD problems across rarefied-to-continuum regimes, with strong efficiency gains near the continuum limit.
method: Decompose the collision term into a Maxwellian relaxation part plus a conservative remainder.
Define a wave component from the local kinetic-horizon equilibrium integral and a particle component as its exact complement.
Solve the resulting closed wave-particle multiscale system with a coupled implicit iteration that updates macroscopic variables and particles alternately.
evidence_signal: The method was tested on shock, Couette, cavity, hypersonic cylinder, and Apollo flows, matching standard schemes in rarefied/transition regimes and Navier–Stokes near continuum, while requiring about 10^3 to >10^4 fewer iterations in the continuum limit.
watch_item: The approach relies on discrete compatibility and an implicit coupled iteration, so implementation must carefully preserve the fixed-point structure and boundary traction treatment.
paper_title: Wave-Particle Decomposition for Kinetic Equations II: Full Boltzmann equation
